pull.title: wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB
pull.body:
Closes #27583.

`PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB` already serializes, deserializes and merges when PSBTs are combined. Nothing writes it, so a PSBT produced by the wallet never carries it, and a signer that only has the file cannot rebuild the multisig from it. Today Specter [fills the field itself](https://github.com/cryptoadvance/specter-desktop/blob/8843e2f0640a9adc129f9ab6afe5ecb9632e7c5b/src/cryptoadvance/specter/wallet/wallet.py#L1866-L1881) after getting the PSBT from Core.

<details><summary>Before and after with the BitBox02 and Trezor simulators</summary>

A 2-of-3 `wsh(sortedmulti(...))` on regtest with the simulator as one co-signer, signed through HWI 3.2.0. The "before" file is the same PSBT with its `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB` records removed, so nothing else differs.

| | without the field | with the field |
|---|---|---|
| BitBox02 | refuses, `This BitBox02 is not one of the cosigners` | signs |
| Trezor T | signs, co-signer nodes sent with zeroed chain codes and no derivation paths | signs, nodes sent with the real chain codes and paths |

What `parse_multisig` hands the Trezor for the change output:

```
without: global xpubs=0  zeroed chain codes=3/3  depths=[0, 0, 0]  paths=[[], [], []]
with   : global xpubs=3  zeroed chain codes=0/3  depths=[4, 4, 4]  paths=[[1, 0], [1, 0], [1, 0]]
```

</details>

A new `Descriptor` accessor returns the extended keys a descriptor is built from, and `DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::FillPSBT` writes those of every descriptor with an input or an output in the PSBT. That covers `walletcreatefundedpsbt`, `walletprocesspsbt`, `send`, `sendall`, `psbtbumpfee` and the GUI send dialog, which all go through `CWallet::FillPSBT`.

Only the keys BIP 174 allows are added, the ones that derive, through unhardened steps alone, a key the PSBT gives a derivation path for. So a key expression ending in `/*h` adds nothing.

Whoever holds a PSBT from the wallet can now derive the addresses of the descriptors it uses. Setting `bip32derivs` to false in `walletcreatefundedpsbt` or `walletprocesspsbt` leaves the field out, along with the derivation paths.

`descriptorprocesspsbt` is left out, since it signs from the descriptors it is given without going through the wallet, and I intend to cover it as a follow-up.

@jeanpablojp in the RP description, can you point to the source code in Specter where it adds the global xpub? This might be useful for those who want to verify that it's still needed. Similarly, it's useful to provide a before and after example flow with HWI (and e.g. a Trezor / simulator).

(It's also better to not to tag people in the PR description, because IIUC that text ends up in the merge commit, which then keeps triggering notifications as other projects backport it.)

Both are in the description now.

The Specter link points at `Wallet.fill_psbt`, pinned to a commit so the line numbers don't drift.

On the flow: I ran the Trezor T simulator first, and it signs the same PSBT with or without the field, same signature, same prompts, same screens. What differs is only the data HWI hands it, since without the field `parse_multisig` fills the co-signer nodes with zeroed chain codes and no derivation paths. The device that does show a difference is the BitBox02: it refuses with `This BitBox02 is not one of the cosigners` and signs once the field is there. Both runs are in the collapsed block.

I had written that the Trezor needed the field. That was wrong, and the description is corrected.

Also dropped the tag, thanks for the note about the merge commit.

Thanks. It's useful to know that Trezor doesn't seem to need this, but BitBox02 and perhaps other devices do.

I suspect that once we support the new `registerdescriptor` command in HWI, and pass that registration back to HWI when signing, none of the devices will need the global xpub. That's because HWI can construct everything it needs from the descriptor, which itself contains the xpubs.

But providing global xpubs may still be useful for flows without HWI.

Please shorten your description. We don't need to know the exact details about every single device that needs to know about the global xpub.

Why is this restricted to only multisigs? Just because that is the described use case in the original issue does not mean that it is the only use case. PSBTs and Descriptors are generic objects, we should avoid doing things that are specific to one type of descriptor or psbt.

@jeanpablojp, in case it saves you time: https://github.com/fametrano/bitcoin/tree/psbt-global-xpub-achow has achow101's points and the NetBSD thread-safety fix, rebased on master.

Changes: the multisig-only restriction is gone. `Descriptor::GetExtPubKeysWithOrigins` returns the map, takes no `SigningProvider`, and falls back to the root key when the cache lacks the last hardened one. `musig()` gives the participants' keys.

There are two commits. The wallet one is yours, with me as co-author. Take any of it or none. To use it as it is: `git fetch https://github.com/fametrano/bitcoin psbt-global-xpub-achow && git reset --hard FETCH_HEAD`, then force-push. A shorter description you could reword is below.

*Written with LLM, a computer and the Internet; the mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

<details><summary>Suggested description</summary>

Closes #27583.

BIP 174 lets a PSBT carry, in `PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB`, the extended public keys its inputs and outputs derive from. The wallet never writes the field. Some signers need them to rebuild the scripts.

`FillPSBT` now adds the extended keys of every descriptor that an input or output uses, unless `bip32derivs` is false. For each key expression this is the key at its last hardened step when the descriptor cache holds it, and the root key otherwise. For `musig()` these are the participants' keys. `descriptorprocesspsbt` does not go through the wallet and is left for a follow-up.

So, by default, a PSBT from the wallet carries the account xpubs of the descriptors it uses, and whoever gets it can derive the wallet's addresses. With hardened ranged derivation (`/*h`) the cache holds no such key, and the root key is published if its origin is known. Keys whose origin is unknown are left out.

</details>

rename.from: wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB for descriptors with more than one key

events.message:
descriptor: add GetExtPubKeysWithOrigins

Give Descriptor a way to hand out the extended public keys it is built
from, each keyed by its origin.

Each BIP 32 key expression gives the key at its last hardened step when
the descriptor cache holds that key, and its root key otherwise. The key
at the last hardened step is the one the expression's unhardened
children derive from. A key origin written in the descriptor takes the
place of the root's fingerprint and is prepended to the path. A musig()
expression hands out its participants' keys, and a plain public key has
none to give.

The keys carry the network's version bytes, since BIP 174 serializes
those bytes as part of each PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB key and a key parsed from a
descriptor lacks them. The wallet starts using this in the next commit.

wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB

BIP 174 lets a PSBT carry the extended public keys that the keys in its
inputs and outputs derive from, so that a signer holding no wallet
state can rebuild the scripts from the PSBT alone. The PSBT code
already serializes, deserializes and merges PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB, but the
wallet never writes it.

Have DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::FillPSBT add the extended keys of every
descriptor that contributed an input or an output, unless bip32derivs
is false. That covers walletcreatefundedpsbt, walletprocesspsbt, send,
sendall, psbtbumpfee and the GUI, which all go through
CWallet::FillPSBT.

Only keys that BIP 174 allows go in. A key has to derive one of the
keys the PSBT gives a derivation path for, through unhardened steps
alone, and its path has to have as many steps as its depth. The first
rule leaves out the root key a descriptor falls back to when its cache
lacks the key at the last hardened step, which is always the case with
/*h derivation. The second leaves out a non-master key written in the
descriptor without its origin.

A PSBT from the wallet now carries the extended keys of the
descriptors it uses, and whoever holds it can derive their addresses.
Setting bip32derivs to false in walletcreatefundedpsbt or
walletprocesspsbt leaves them out, along with the derivation paths.

The BIP 174 updater test vector now carries the extended keys of its
descriptors.

events.body:
@achow101 thanks, shortened the description and dropped the multisig restriction.

@fametrano thanks for the branch. The single-key test over the four address types follows yours. Unlike your branch, keys that derive none of the PSBT's keys stay out, like the root of a `/*h` expression, which in a migrated legacy wallet is the master key.

comments.body:
In 92bf732c4ee0e7096aa3f203ebcafcdf9366ff1a "wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB for descriptors with more than one key"

This should return the map rather than taking it as an output parameter.

Do not provide `SigningProvider`, either the last hardened key is already cached, or it does not exist. There is no need to take a `SigningProvider` here, otherwise the wallet wouldn't function.

In 92bf732c4ee0e7096aa3f203ebcafcdf9366ff1a "wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB for descriptors with more than one key"

We should not make assumptions about what the caller is going to use the xpubs for. This should return the root and it's fingerprint for any key where we cannot do the normalized key thing.

In 92bf732c4ee0e7096aa3f203ebcafcdf9366ff1a "wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB for descriptors with more than one key"

It is not necessary to determine what the last hardened index is, just ask the cache for it, and if the cache doesn't have that key, return the root.

In 92bf732c4ee0e7096aa3f203ebcafcdf9366ff1a "wallet: fill PSBT_GLOBAL_XPUB for descriptors with more than one key"

This is incorrect. It should traverse the participants and get their xpubs.
Done, it returns the map and takes only the cache.

Done, it now returns the root and its fingerprint, `/*h` included. What goes in the PSBT is up to the wallet, which follows BIP 174's definition of the field and only adds keys that derive, through unhardened steps alone, a key the PSBT gives a derivation path for. So with `/*h` the root still stays out of the PSBT.
Done, it asks the cache and falls back to the root. The origin path comes from the cached key's depth, so `LastHardenedIndex` and the `refactor:` commit that extracted it are gone.
Right, done. It now merges whatever its participants return, and `wallet_musig.py` checks that every participant's xpub ends up in `global_xpubs` with the origin that leads to it.
